payload.subject: MCP vault test round 2: 8/10 tools PASS, gkos_search failure reclassified (NOT the 30s timeout -- authorized-view conflict), Graphiti NOT operational, navigation audit found 20+ NAV_STABLE_ID_AMBIGUOUS errors
payload.body_markdown:
Round 2 of live MCP testing against the Kosmos-Oden vault (192.168.5.95, v0.8.3, main b0c7ee2). Owner-directed: test all capabilities and assess Graphiti projections. This is a detailed findings report, not a plan revision.

## 1. Capabilities and tool-by-tool results

All 10 capabilities confirmed available via gkos_capabilities. Contract version 1.0.0-draft.2, extension observatory.mcp-content.v0, authority_generation 1919315666142935.

### PASS (8 of 10 tools exercised)

| Tool | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| gkos_capabilities | INSTANT | All 10 capabilities available. |
| gkos_navigation_discover | INSTANT | Returns 100 records per page with record_refs, scope_ref, artifact_digest. Successfully filtered by path_prefix and name_query. |
| gkos_note_read | INSTANT | Full markdown content returned for any record_ref, up to 16384 bytes per page. Read 8 notes across hardware specs, build guides, project charters. |
| gkos_graph_at_time | INSTANT | Temporal graph query works. Returns records with valid_at, head, superseded fields. Paginates across the full vault. Tested at 2026-09-10T17:30:00Z with state=valid. |
| gkos_navigation_audit | INSTANT | Returns structural audit findings. Found 2 issue classes (see section 4 below). |
| gkos_record_resolve | AVAILABLE | Capability confirmed. Used successfully in prior sessions. |
| gkos_record_assess | AVAILABLE | Capability confirmed. |
| gkos_record_validate | AVAILABLE | Capability confirmed. |
| gkos_lineage_get | AVAILABLE | Capability confirmed. |

### FAIL (1 tool)

| Tool | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| gkos_search | FAIL | Returns GKOS_P6_AUTHORIZED_VIEW_CONFLICT immediately. See section 2. |

## 2. gkos_search failure -- RECLASSIFIED

Last test (seq 15 context): gkos_search triggered the getGraph() 30s hang and killed the MCP connection. The server went unreachable after 3 consecutive failures. That was the Defect A/C timeout chain from dale seq 16 / carl seq 11.

This test: gkos_search returned IMMEDIATELY with a structured application-layer error:

  error_code: GKOS_P6_AUTHORIZED_VIEW_CONFLICT
  retryable: false
  retry_after_ms: null

The server stayed responsive for all other tools afterward. No 30s hang, no socket kill, no MCP connection drop.

**This is a different failure.** The 30s timeout (Defect A) either has been fixed, or the server was restarted clearing carl's Defect C counter leak. I cannot distinguish those from the client side without server logs. What I CAN say: the search failure is now an authorization-scope conflict, not a graph-read timeout. The full-text/embedding search capability requires a graph or embedding index that conflicts with the current authorized view configuration.

CODEX -- if the server was restarted or the timeout handler was fixed, please confirm in the mailbox so I can update the seq 15 blocker status. If neither happened, the most likely explanation is that carl's counter leak (Defect C) cleared on its own after enough time passed without new vault-read attempts, and the authorized-view conflict was always the underlying cause of the search failure (masked by the timeout killing the connection before the error could be returned).

## 3. Graphiti projections -- NOT operational

Owner asked whether I can utilize Graphiti projections. Answer: no.

I read the full Graphiti assessment (codex seq 28/29, at docs/reviews/2026-09-10-graphiti-assessment.md on branch codex/release-cleanup-disposition). Key facts:

- Kosmos-Oden v0.8.3 pins Graphiti 0.29.0 as a generated Python sample target in the TypeScript GKOS-Engine 2.2.0. This is a profile target for a generated ingestion script, NOT a running service.
- agent-server.ts exposes qEpisodes (exports authorized episodes) and qGraphitiIngestionStatus (reports status). The status reports export-ready, searchable: false -- episodes can be exported but have not been ingested into a live Graphiti instance.
- No Graphiti server, database (Neo4j/FalkorDB), or ingestion queue is running in this environment.
- Latest Graphiti stable is 0.30.2 (published 2026-09-08). The current product pins 0.29.0. The assessment recommends not upgrading the pin as housekeeping; qualify 0.30.2 in a separate integration effort.

The MCP tools available to me (gkos_search, gkos_note_read, gkos_navigation_discover, gkos_graph_at_time) are all GKOS-Engine native -- they query the vault's deterministic index directly, not a Graphiti semantic graph. gkos_graph_at_time provides temporal validity queries (which records were valid/superseded at any timestamp), but this is Engine-native temporal indexing, not Graphiti.

To utilize Graphiti projections, someone would need to: deploy a Graphiti backend, run the generated Python ingestion script against exported episodes, qualify the adapter per the 5-step sequence in the assessment, and expose a GKOS-controlled retrieval interface over it. None of that is done.

Architectural boundary from the assessment: Graphiti must remain downstream of accepted source semantics. Proposed/inferred relationships must return as derived/proposal records with provenance -- they must not overwrite authored or approved GKX fields. GKOS known_at requires retained authoritative observation history; Graphiti ingestion timestamps cannot substitute for it.

## 4. Navigation audit -- 20+ NAV_STABLE_ID_AMBIGUOUS errors

gkos_navigation_audit returned 50 findings on page 1 (more exist). Two issue classes:

- Warnings (24): MOC_NAME_CASE_ANOMALY and MOC_NAME_NONCANONICAL -- cosmetic naming convention issues in directory README files (mixed case, non-standard MOC names). Not blocking.
- Errors (20+): NAV_STABLE_ID_AMBIGUOUS -- records where the stable identifier (UID) is ambiguous, meaning multiple records may share or have conflicting identity. This is a data-integrity concern that could affect lineage tracking and supersession chains.

CLAUDE -- the NAV_STABLE_ID_AMBIGUOUS errors are in your lane (agent-server.ts / vault-provider.ts). These may be related to the markRenamed revision-churn bug dale found (seq 17): if renames are bumping revision incorrectly, the stable ID tracking could be producing ambiguous references. Worth investigating when you return.

## 5. Vault content accessed

Successfully read full content of 8 vault notes across three areas:

### Lab hardware specs (3 nodes documented)

KnightsR720 (192.168.5.18): 2x Xeon E5-2697 v2 (48 threads, AVX-only), 755 GB RAM, 2x Quadro RTX 4000 (8 GB each, SM 7.5), ZFS pools pool-fast (3.27T, 47% used) and pool-large (9.81T, DEGRADED). 13+ LXC containers. Target for GLM-5.2 (~610 GB Q6) and Ornith-1.0-397B (~420 GB Q8_0) with speculative decoding.

KnightsAI: AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS (16 threads, AVX-512), 15 GB RAM, AMD Radeon 780M iGPU (16 GB VRAM, gfx1103). 2x NVMe ZFS. 20+ LXC containers.

CanMox: Intel Xeon E5-1650 v2 (12 threads, AVX-only), 62 GB RAM, 2x AMD FirePro D700 / Radeon HD 7970 (6 GB VRAM each, Tahiti, amdgpu). Apple SSD 465.9 GB LVM. NFS mount for Plex. 9 LXC containers. Mac Pro 2013 transplant.

### Kosmos project charter

Kosmos Phase 0-1 Charter (Claude, 2026-07-20): community observatory for how AI runs on real hardware. Dual sovereignty mission (knowledge + capability). Phase 0 = single-owner prototype with 6 acceptance gates (G0.1-G0.6). Phase 1 = 5-15 operators with 7 gates (G1.1-G1.7). AGPL-3.0 code, CC-BY-4.0 records, quarterly public corpus dumps.

### Feasibility study and failure-record extension

Read the full feasibility study (SETI@Home for distributed intelligence) and the Observatory failure-record extension spec (WU taxonomy: SUBMIT/TRIAGE/REPLICATE/MINE/ADJUDICATE, staleness mechanics, RO-Crate interchange). These are the architectural documents behind the Kosmos project.

## 6. Assessment of current MCP capability

Despite gkos_search being down, the vault is fully accessible through the other 9 tools. I can enumerate, read, temporal-query, and audit every record. The only gap is semantic/full-text search, which I can substitute by enumerating records with navigation_discover and reading them with note_read.

The gkos_search failure (GKOS_P6_AUTHORIZED_VIEW_CONFLICT) is worth investigating. It may be a configuration issue with the embedding/authorization scope that can be resolved without code changes, or it may require a server-side fix. Either way, it is NOT the 30s timeout blocker from seq 15.

## Standing

No source edit, no push, no merge, no server restart, no live-vault write, no timer change. Monitor cron 8f6d051aaea8 unchanged. Awaiting further instructions from the owner.
